title: Chronic theobromine administration attenuates short-term memory decline via neurotrophic, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant mechanisms in senescence-accelerated mouse prone 8 (SAMP8).
authors: Sumiyoshi, Eri; Matsuzaki, Kentaro; Katakura, Masanori; Nazib, Shadman; Hossain, Shahdat; Maejima, Sho; Zhang, Ying; Kishi, Hiroko; Sugimoto, Naotoshi; Shido, Osamu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究可可碱对衰老小鼠记忆衰退的神经保护作用，涉及分子对接但对象为小分子-酶互作，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA体系无关。
abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline is a major concern in aging societies. Theobromine (TB), a cacao-derived methylxanthine, exerts neuroprotective effects through anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neurotrophic mechanisms; however, its efficacy in aging models remains unclear. This study investigated the mechanisms underlying neuroprotective effects of chronic TB administration in senescence-accelerated mouse prone 8 (SAMP8), a model of age-related memory impairment. SAMP8 and SAMR1 mice were fed either a control diet or a diet supplemented with 0.05% TB for 50 d. Cognitive performance was evaluated by the novel object recognition (NOR) test. Neurotrophic factors (BDNF and NT-3), synaptic proteins (PSD95 and synaptophysin), and plasticity-related signaling molecules (phosphorylated CREB and TrkB) were analyzed in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. Inflammatory cytokines, lipid peroxides, and antioxidant enzymes were quantified. Molecular docking was used to assess TB's interaction with phosphodiesterase (PDE) enzymes. TB improved short-term memory in SAMP8, increasing discrimination index in the NOR test. This was accompanied by increased BDNF, NT-3, PSD95, and synaptophysin levels and enhanced CREB and TrkB phosphorylation. Furthermore, TB lowered the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, TNF-alpha) and phosphorylated NF-kappaB, reduced lipid peroxidation, and increased the levels of antioxidant markers (HO-1, GSH). These effects were minimal in SAMR1. No adverse effects on body weight or blood parameters were observed. Molecular docking indicated that TB binds to PDE enzymes with weaker inhibitory activity than selective inhibitors. TB enhances short-term memory and synaptic function in aged mice via neurotrophic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory mechanisms, supporting its potential as a safe dietary intervention for age-related cognitive decline.
abstract_zh: 与衰老相关的认知功能下降是老龄化社会中的一个主要问题。可可来源的甲基黄嘌呤——可可碱 (Theobromine, TB)，通过抗炎、抗氧化和神经营养机制发挥神经保护作用；然而，其在衰老模型中的疗效仍不明确。本研究探讨了慢性TB给药在衰老加速小鼠易感8 (senescence-accelerated mouse prone 8, SAMP8) 模型中神经保护作用的机制，该模型是年龄相关记忆障碍的模型。SAMP8和SAMR1小鼠分别喂食对照饮食或补充0.05% TB的饮食，持续50天。通过新物体识别 (novel object recognition, NOR) 测试评估认知表现。在前额叶皮层和海马中分析了神经营养因子 (BDNF和NT-3)、突触蛋白 (PSD95和突触素) 以及可塑性相关信号分子 (磷酸化CREB和TrkB)。定量了炎症细胞因子、脂质过氧化物和抗氧化酶。使用分子对接评估TB与磷酸二酯酶 (phosphodiesterase, PDE) 酶的相互作用。TB改善了SAMP8的短期记忆，提高了NOR测试中的辨别指数。这伴随着BDNF、NT-3、PSD95和突触素水平的增加，以及CREB和TrkB磷酸化的增强。此外，TB降低了促炎细胞因子 (IL-1beta、TNF-alpha) 和磷酸化NF-kappaB的水平，减少了脂质过氧化，并增加了抗氧化标志物 (HO-1、GSH) 的水平。这些效应在SAMR1中最小。未观察到对体重或血液参数的不良影响。分子对接表明，TB与PDE酶结合，其抑制活性弱于选择性抑制剂。TB通过神经营养、抗氧化和抗炎机制增强老年小鼠的短期记忆和突触功能，支持其作为年龄相关认知功能下降的安全饮食干预措施的潜力。
